On peggit I often see people ask, "how can I get moar flexible? anybody got a flexibility rooteen??? :("

This made me want to write a general primer on flexibility.

Getting stretchy is not hard, people have been getting absurdly flexible for thousands of years without any gear or special techniques. Dancers, acrobats, martial artists...

> How do I stretch?

There's basically 3 good techniques:

1. Static stretching. You hold a position for a long time trying to breathe into it and get more comfortable in it.

2. Dynamic stretching. You move through a range of motion trying to gradually move further from workout to workout.

3. External resistance. There's a variety of ways people do this. Partner stretches, using weights, rope/strap devices...

Which one do you use? Probably dynamic stretching. It's simple, does not require a lot of time (I'm too impatient for static anymore) and gets results for most people. If you're not stretching what you want to stretch with a dynamic stretch then maybe you need to change movements, try static stretching or try something with external resistance. Bottom line, screw around with it until something starts working. No matter what your problem is, one of those three methods is GOING to solve it because that's all there is.

> When should I stretch?

Generally, off days and after exercise. Some people stretch a little before exercise, but others are paranoid that slackens their joints and puts them at risk for injury. If you stretch before exercise, you probably want to go light and just "limber up" rather than try to hit some kind of flexibility personal record. Use your best judgment, it isn't rocket science.

> What stretches should I do? Can you recommend a flexibility routine?

This is where people get screwed and way overcomplicated. Flexibility is a *specific* trait. There is no such thing as a person who is flexible "in general," therefore no general flexibility routine exists. You have to decide what joints you want to be flexible, and in which directions. You basically have your axial spine (neck, ribcage and lumbar spine), then your shoulders and hips, then your elbows and knees, then ankles and wrists. That's pretty much what there is to stretch.

It is now **up to you** to decide which of those joints should be more mobile and in which directions.

This is difficult for most people, because most people in fitness *have no idea what they're trying to accomplish.* In general, for most people I would start with the **shoulders, hips, wrists and ankles.** You don't want to dick with your axial spine too much, though you don't want to be stiff you also probably are best off not trying to be a contortionist. There is such a thing as too much flexibility, especially in the spine.

> Okay, so what do I do?

Rather than follow any specific espoused routine, I suggest you go on youtube and find your own stretches for the various functions of those joints. Even better than doing your own bodily maintenance is to *learn about your own body,* and use *your own research and judgment* as to what it needs.

For the people who just want to get flexible, your homework is to get on youtube, look up "leg stretches," "shoulder stretches," "ankle stretches," "wrist stretches" etcetera and just try some of them out. See what works for you and get after it.
